# Summary

The manifesto outlines a comprehensive policy platform focused on economic, social, and governmental reform.

## Economic Policy

The document presents plans to create a fairer economy through a £250 billion National Transformation Fund for infrastructure investment over ten years, including transport, broadband, and energy systems. Industrial strategy would establish regional development banks and a National Investment Bank to support lending. The tax approach proposes no increases for those earning under £80,000 annually, with higher contributions from top earners and corporations. The fiscal framework commits to eliminating day-to-day spending deficits within five years while investing in growth.

## Public Ownership

Significant nationalization is proposed, including railways (as franchises expire), energy networks, water systems, and postal services. These measures aim to reduce costs and improve accountability.

## Public Services

The NHS would receive £30 billion in additional funding, with guarantees on waiting times and staffing levels. A National Care Service would address social care funding with £8 billion additional investment. A National Education Service would provide free education from early years through university, abolishing tuition fees and restoring maintenance grants.

## Employment

Workers' rights would expand through banning zero-hours contracts, ending the public sector pay cap, raising minimum wage, and strengthening trade union powers. A new twenty-point employment rights plan addresses issues from paternity leave to workplace protections.

## Housing

Over one million homes would be built, including 100,000 council and housing association homes annually. Rent controls, longer tenancies, and measures against homelessness are proposed.

## Brexit

The approach prioritizes economic access to European markets, protecting workers' rights and environmental standards, guaranteeing EU nationals' rights, and ensuring parliamentary oversight of negotiations.

## Social Security

Reforms include maintaining pension protections, scrapping certain benefit cuts, and reforming disability assessments to be more supportive rather than punitive.

## International Affairs

Foreign policy emphasizes diplomacy, human rights, and international cooperation, maintaining defense spending commitments while supporting nuclear non-proliferation efforts. Development spending would continue at 0.7% of national income.
